input.content:
# Review — Component User Stories & the Contentful ⇄ PWA Kit Dependency

**Prepared for:** "Contentful v PWA Kit Components and User Story Alignment" (Isabel Chaloner, Tim Lavelle)
**Date:** 2026-08-12 · **Reviewer:** Marcel Navarro (FE lead)
**Scope reviewed:** Confluence 04.71 (the assumed standard) · Confluence 04.7 Component Inventory · the six sample stories (SFCC-698/699/700, SFCC-92/648/650) · the earlier example set (SFCC-691/692/694) · Jira epic structure · the two pre-existing story standards · `.docs/integration/02-contentful.md` · the actual Contentful integration code in this repo.

---

## 1. Verdict

**The taxonomy in 04.71 is sound and worth adopting. The worked example chosen to demonstrate it (Editorial Cards) does not follow it, and — more importantly — the dependency direction 04.71 assumes is backwards for roughly half the Contentful components in this codebase.**

Three things need deciding before this pattern is rolled out across Sprint 3's story-writing effort:

1. **Which Contentful integration pattern a component uses** determines whether the Contentful story comes before or after the PWA Kit story. 04.71 assumes one order; the code supports two. (§4 — this is the substantive finding.)
2. **The Contentful story and the PWA Kit story need a shared, explicit field contract** or they cannot be worked independently. None of the six samples has one. (§5.2)
3. **Existing monolithic page stories (SFCC-90, SFCC-94) already cover the same ground** as the new Level-2 example. Adopting 04.71 without deciding what happens to them creates duplicate scope. (§7.2)

The best story in the sample set is **SFCC-648** — it is the only one with complete metadata and a named, owned dependency. It should be the template, not Editorial Cards.

---

## 2. What 04.71 gets right

Worth stating plainly, because most of this review is corrections:

- The two-level split (component epic / page epic) is the correct decomposition and matches where this codebase's test layers naturally sit (§8.3).
- "A Contentful component always needs a PWA Kit story too, because PWA Kit has to render it" is exactly right and is the single most useful sentence on the page.
- Writing Level-2 from the shopper's perspective, and explicitly *not* repeating build detail, is the right instinct.
- The classification is already pre-populated in 04.7 Component Inventory's "PWA Kit / Contentful" column, so the standard has a data source to drive it. That's more than most story conventions start with.

---

## 3. The sample stories — defect table

Verified against the two pre-existing standards (Confluence 274137093 *Creating User Stories with Claude* v11, and 277577757 *Guide 1: Writing Stories & AC*).

| # | Story | Finding | Severity |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | SFCC-698/699/700 | **All three sit in epic SFCC-2 "PWA Kit Components"** (verified `parent` field, not just the description text). Per 04.71, SFCC-698 belongs in **SFCC-304 Contentful Components** and SFCC-700 in a page epic (**SFCC-706 Homepage**, created 2026-08-12). Both target epics already exist. | High |
| 2 | SFCC-698 | **8 of 10 AC are render assertions, not content-model assertions.** AC2–AC8 are all phrased "*When the component renders on the storefront → Then …*". 04.71 assigns rendering to the PWA Kit story and the content model / authoring fields / validation rules to the Contentful story. The example inverts its own rule, and duplicates SFCC-699. | **High** |
| 3 | SFCC-698 | **The content model cannot express the four variants the Inventory lists.** 04.7 records Editorial Cards variants as *Editorial Cards / 2 Columns / Centered Text / 2 Columns Centered Text* — a 2×2 matrix of column-count × text-alignment. AC1 defines a single `Layout: Standard \| Centred text` enum and **no column-count field**. As specified, 2-column is unbuildable. | **High** |
| 4 | SFCC-698 | **No field defines the card collection.** AC1 lists one card's fields (single Image, single Body copy); AC3 requires "two cards side by side, each with their own independently configured content". Nothing in the model says whether Editorial Cards is a container holding 1–2 card entries, or one entry with duplicated field sets. This is the decision that blocks development. | **High** |
| 5 | SFCC-698 | **AC1 and AC9 both cite SFCC-691 for the Title and Link dependency.** SFCC-691 is the *PWA Kit render* story; **SFCC-692** is the Contentful content-model story. A content-model dependency must point at SFCC-692. | Medium |
| 6 | SFCC-698 | **An open question is embedded inside AC1**: "Image (required) — *from Contentful for editorial?*". Per 274137093 open items belong in Dependencies (`customfield_10232`) with a named owner, never inline in AC. Same defect in SFCC-692's description ("TBC: are these responsive designs, or different configurations?"). | Medium |
| 7 | SFCC-699 | **AC1 is a compound assertion covering ~16 combinations** — 4 fields × 2 layouts × 2 alignments in one criterion. Guide 1 lists "Compound Then" as a named common mistake: *"One failure masks the others in test results."* Needs splitting. | Medium |
| 8 | SFCC-699 | **No AC for Contentful being unavailable, or for a missing/unpublished entry.** `02-contentful.md` §8 mandates specific behaviour (editorial slots render empty, commerce never blocked; asset 404 → alt text + graceful placeholder), and AGENTS.md requires each external system to fail independently. Absent from the render story. | **High** |
| 9 | SFCC-699 | **No AC for image performance.** `02-contentful.md` §6 requires AVIF/WebP via the Images API, `srcset`/`sizes` per breakpoint, lazy-loading below the fold, `fetchpriority="high"` on the largest hero. AGENTS.md sets LCP ≤ 2s p75 mobile. A full-width editorial image module is squarely on that budget. | **High** |
| 10 | SFCC-700 | **Page contradiction.** Summary says "Homepage Template"; the story sentence says "*As a shopper browsing the product listing page*"; all four AC say homepage. SFCC-698 meanwhile scopes the component to "the Home page and PLP" — which under 04.71 requires **two** Level-2 stories, one per page. Only one exists, and it names the wrong page. | High |
| 11 | SFCC-700 | **AC3 is internally contradictory**: "*16px spacing between the Editorial Card and the footer **above***". AC2 already places the category component above. The footer is below. | Low |
| 12 | SFCC-700 | **Hardcoded pixel values (40px, 16px) in AC.** `.claude/rules/css.md` forbids hardcoded spacing values — spacing comes from theme tokens (`overrides/app/theme/foundation/spacing.ts`, Tier 1). AC should name the token, or dev must either violate the rule or reverse-engineer which token equals 40px. | Medium |
| 13 | SFCC-698/699/700 | **`Functional Area`, `Squad`, `Rollout Scope` and `Dependencies` are all empty on all three** (verified). 274137093 lists each as mandatory. Compare SFCC-648: Functional Area `PDP`, Squad `Squad A`, Rollout Scope all 8 storefronts, Dependencies a specific @Kiera Figma request. | High |
| 14 | SFCC-698/699/700/691/692/694 | **No labels at all** — so no Req ID traceability (`HPC-…`/`PRD-…`), no `Custom`/`Config`, no `Squad-…`, no `Contentful`. Every real story carries these; SFCC-111 uses exactly `Contentful;Custom;HPC-017;Squad-A`. Without Req IDs these stories are invisible to the 04.1.x requirements-coverage trace. | High |
| 15 | SFCC-698/699/700 | **`**Epic:** PWA Kit Components` is written into the Description.** 274137093: the description must contain *only* the user story and context; epic is a field. SFCC-700 additionally has broken escaping (`\*\*Epic:\*\*`) so it renders as literal asterisks. | Low |
| 16 | SFCC-698 | Persona is "*merchandiser*"; the canonical persona in 04.3 / 274137093 is **Site Merchandiser** (as used correctly in SFCC-111 and SFCC-94). | Low |
| 17 | SFCC-699/700 | **No region tagging.** Guide 1: *"Always tag, even if the answer is [ALL]."* With one Contentful Space serving 8 storefronts across 11 locales (`02-contentful.md` §7) and the `regions` filtering field still an **open item** (§10.1), an untagged editorial component is a real ambiguity, not a formality. | Medium |
| 18 | SFCC-92/648/650 | **This set is materially better** and largely already complies. SFCC-92 was correctly thinned to page-level assembly and left in SFCC-5; 648/650 were split into SFCC-2 as component stories — exactly 04.71's model, arrived at independently in the SFCC-92 thread (Tim Lavelle 2026-07-26 → Jasmijn Tsang 2026-08-07). One correction: SFCC-648's description commits to **WCAG 2.1 AA**, but AGENTS.md targets **2.2 AA**, falling back to 2.1 only where 2.2 is infeasible *and documented*. | Medium |

---

## 4. The substantive finding — dependency direction is not uniform

04.71 states the Contentful story covers "the content model, authoring fields, configuration options and validation rules" and the PWA Kit story covers "how the component renders and responds to what Contentful delivers". That implies: **Contentful model first → PWA Kit renders it.**

That is correct for one of the two Contentful patterns in this repo, and backwards for the other.

### Pattern A — entry-driven components
`overrides/app/components/contentful/` — `heroBanner.tsx`, `duplexSection.tsx`, `videoEmbed.tsx`, `productHero.tsx`

- Receive a **typed Contentful entry/asset** as a prop (`ContentfulAsset` from `overrides/app/types/contentful`).
- Content types are defined in code and synced via `npm run sync:contentful` (`scripts/contentful/content-types/`, `scripts/contentful/migrations/`).
- Live Preview wiring is per-field: `ContentfulLivePreview.getProps({entryId, fieldId, locale})`.
- **The Contentful content model is genuinely upstream. 04.71's ordering is correct.**
- Critical constraint: `02-contentful.md` §2 — the sync script is **additive only, it never deletes a field from a live content type**. Getting the model wrong is expensive and semi-permanent. This is the strongest possible argument for reviewing the Contentful story *against real component prop needs* before it is built.

### Pattern B — Studio Experiences components
`overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/` — `collectionHero.tsx`, `imageText.tsx`, `shoppableImage.tsx`

- The authoring model is **generated from the React component's props**. You annotate the `Props` type with `@cf` JSDoc tags and run `npm run generate:contentful`, which rewrites `definitions.ts` (autogenerated; a pre-commit hook keeps it in sync).
- So the "content model / authoring fields" **are an output of writing the React component**, not an input to it. For these components 04.71's ordering is inverted.
- **And the available controls are severely limited.** `scripts/contentful/generateDefinitions.mjs` `CONTROL_MAP` supports exactly six: `shortText`, `longText`, `select`, `toggle`, `number`, `media` → mapping only to Contentful `Text`, `Boolean`, `Number`, `Media`.
  - **No reference/link control** → the "Title and Link sub-component (optional)" in SFCC-698 AC1 is not expressible.
  - **No array/repeater control** → "two cards, each independently configured" is not expressible.
  - **No rich text control.**
  - The existing workaround is visible and unattractive: `shoppableImage` degrades structured hotspot data to a **`Hotspots (JSON)` Text field** in Studio (a merchandiser hand-typing JSON), while the *content-type* version of the same component models it properly as an `Object`.
  - The one supported composition primitive is `children` → `children: true` on the registration. A 2-column Editorial Cards is therefore most naturally **a container component with two child slots**, each holding a single Editorial Card — not one entry with a layout enum.

### Why this matters for the meeting

**Editorial Cards as specified in SFCC-698 cannot be built as a Studio Experiences component today.** It needs either the entry-driven path with proper entry references, or re-decomposition into `editorialCard` + a layout container. That is a story-shape decision, not an implementation detail, and it has to be made before the story is estimated.

**Recommendation:** add a third column to the 04.71 quick-reference and to 04.7 Component Inventory — not just *PWA Kit / Contentful*, but *which Contentful pattern*: `Entry-driven` or `Studio Experiences`. Then:

| Pattern | Story order | Contentful story delivers | PWA Kit story delivers |
|---|---|---|---|
| Entry-driven | **Contentful first**, PWA Kit second | Content type in `content-types/` + migration, field IDs, validation, locale/region behaviour | Typed component consuming the entry, all render states |
| Studio Experiences | **PWA Kit first** (build against mock content in Storybook), Contentful second | `@cf` annotations reviewed, `definitions.ts` regenerated, Studio registration verified | Component + props, which *are* the authoring surface |

The project has already been doing the second one informally and correctly: **SFCC-51** built the Promotional Announcement Banner UI with mock content, and **SFCC-111** followed up with "the Contentful content model and the integration between Contentful and the PWA Kit component". SFCC-90 and SFCC-94 both say the component "can be built with mock content prior to Contentful content model being finalised." 04.71 should **codify that existing practice**, not contradict it.

> One guardrail worth writing into the DoD: mock Contentful content belongs in the `.stories.tsx` file only (`.claude/rules/components.md` explicitly endorses this for the `Contentful/` story category). AGENTS.md's "No mocking" rule still bars fixtures from production paths.

---

## 5. What's missing from 04.71

### 5.1 No AC format, no field guidance, no template
04.71 defines *how many* stories and *whose perspective*, but not what a story must contain. The result is visible in the samples: six exemplars with no labels, no Functional Area, no Squad, no Rollout Scope, no Dependencies, and an AC format (`**AC1 — title**` + Given/When/Then bullets) that matches neither existing standard. 04.71 should either adopt one of the two existing formats by reference or explicitly supersede them (§6).

### 5.2 The missing artefact — the field-ID contract
This is the highest-value addition and it directly answers "we are not 100% clear on how to structure these."

`02-contentful.md` §2: *"Each content type pairs with a typed React component. TypeScript types match the Contentful field IDs exactly, so schema drift is caught at compile time."*

That exact-match requirement is a **hard interface between the two stories** and neither SFCC-698 nor SFCC-699 records it — they use prose display names ("Body copy") with no field IDs. Every Contentful component pair should carry an identical table in both stories:

| Field ID | Display name | Type / control | Required | Localised | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `image` | Image | Media | Yes | No | |
| `imageAlt` | Image Alt Text | shortText | No | Yes | empty → `alt=""` |
| `bodyCopy` | Body Copy | longText | No | Yes | |
| `ctaLabel` | CTA Label | shortText | No | Yes | CTA renders only if label **and** URL set |
| `ctaUrl` | CTA URL | shortText | No | No | internal → same tab; external → `_blank` + `rel="noopener noreferrer"` |
| `textAlignment` | Text Alignment | select (`standard` \| `centred`) | Yes (default `standard`) | No | |

Once this table exists and is agreed, the Contentful story and the PWA Kit story are genuinely independently workable — which is the whole point of splitting them. Without it they will drift, and with an additive-only sync script the drift is expensive.

### 5.3 Sub-components are unaddressed
04.7 Inventory uses a `↳ Sub-component` type (Pause/Play, Footer Item, Image Gallery, Wishlist Icon…). 04.71 is silent on them. This repo's own convention already answers it — `.claude/rules/components.md`: *"Not required for purely internal sub-components that only render inside one parent… Cover their variants via the parent's stories."* Recommend: **sub-components do not get their own story unless they are independently reusable**; otherwise they are AC on the parent. Without this rule the Footer alone generates four stories (Footer, Footer Item, Footer Textfield, Icons).

### 5.4 The Inventory's vocabulary doesn't match the taxonomy
04.71 defines two component types. 04.7's column uses three values inconsistently: `PWA Kit`, `Contentful`, and — for Link only — `PWA Kit & Contentful`. But per 04.71 *every* Contentful component also needs a PWA Kit story, so Banner, Footer, Navigation, Editorial Cards, Title and Link, Logo Masthead and Disclaimer (all marked plain `Contentful`) each need two stories. The column that should mechanically tell a BA how many stories to write currently doesn't. Recommend aligning the Inventory to 04.71's exact labels: `PWA Kit only` / `Contentful + PWA Kit`.

### 5.5 Inventory data gaps that block story writing
- **Editorial Cards has `Pages: —`** — the component being used as the worked example has no page mapping, so you cannot derive which Level-2 stories are needed. (SFCC-698 says Home + PLP; SFCC-700 says Homepage; neither is in the Inventory.)
- **Editorial Cards and Title and Link are both 🟠 Not Confirmed** in design status — a component with unconfirmed designs was chosen as the pattern exemplar.
- **Templates table covers only Shell and PDP.** Homepage and PLP templates are absent, yet Level-2 stories are being written against both.

---

## 6. Governance collision — four overlapping standards

04.71 does not reference, and partially conflicts with, three existing pages:

| Page | Status | Conflict with 04.71 / the samples |
|---|---|---|
| **274137093 Creating User Stories with Claude** (v11, Jul 2026) | Detailed, field-level, actively used | Mandates Description = story + context only (samples put Epic in the description); AC as numbered `1. Given/When/Then` in `customfield_10231`; labels `Req-ID;Custom;Squad-X`; Functional Area / Squad / Rollout Scope / Dependencies all required. Samples satisfy none of these. |
| **277577757 Guide 1: Writing Stories & AC** (v2) | Zephyr-facing, defines the `AC Approved` gate | Prescribes a **different Description template entirely** (User Role / Goal / Context / In Scope / Out of Scope / Regions / Edge Cases / Story Key) and a different AC format (`AC-01: title [REGION]`). Samples match neither this nor 274137093. |
| **313884676 Definition of Done** | Applies to both squads | Requires "API Contracts Tested" and "Documentation updated". For a Contentful pair, "API contract" = the field-ID table in §5.2. Worth naming explicitly. |
| **400195600 04.71** | New | Adds a taxonomy but no format; silent on the above. |

**Recommendation:** 04.71 should state in one line that it governs *decomposition only* (how many stories, which epic, whose perspective) and that story *format* remains 274137093 + Guide 1. Then reconcile those two with each other separately — that conflict predates this meeting and is worth its own decision.

### One scope boundary to handle carefully
274137093 lists **"Content authoring in Contentful"** under *"Flag the following in open items but do not build"* (Accenture scope ends at SFCC + PWA Kit + SFCC-side integrations).

This does **not** invalidate 04.71's Contentful story — building the content *model* is in scope (`02-contentful.md` §2 puts schema in this repo, PR-reviewed). But SFCC-698 is phrased as an authoring activity by a Zimmermann persona ("*As a merchandiser, I want to configure Editorial Card modules in Contentful*"), which straddles the line. Recommend 04.71 add: **the Contentful story's deliverable is the content type + Studio registration, not authored entries.** The Site Merchandiser persona describes the capability being enabled; DoD is "content type deployed, component registered and configurable in Studio", never "content authored".

---

## 7. Backlog structure

### 7.1 Epic distribution is inverted
| Epic | Children | Note |
|---|---|---|
| **SFCC-2 PWA Kit Components** | 10 | **6 are EXAMPLE stories.** Only 4 real: SFCC-116, SFCC-236, SFCC-648, SFCC-650 |
| **SFCC-304 Contentful Components** | 4 | SFCC-306, 316, 326, 674 — and *none* of the Contentful exemplars |
| **SFCC-706 Homepage** | 7 | Created 2026-08-12 |

The component epics are nearly empty while page epics hold the real work — i.e. the codebase is currently organised the *old* way, and 04.71 describes a target state that hasn't been migrated to. That migration is the actual Sprint 3 task, and it is much larger than writing three example stories.

Housekeeping: the six `EXAMPLE:` stories are documentation living in a delivery epic. They will be picked up by sprint reports and epic burn-up. Move them to a dedicated epic, label them `example`, or convert them to a Confluence child page of 04.71.

### 7.2 Duplication with existing stories — needs a decision
**SFCC-90 "Homepage Layout & Content Modules UI"** (In Refinement, HPC-008/009, Shopper persona) already enumerates every homepage module top-to-bottom, ending with:

> *"Editorial and/or boutique duo — a final row containing two equal-width (for desktop) hero images side by side: one linking to an editorial destination and one linking to the boutiques page or store locator."*

That is the 2-Column Editorial Card, in the same page position SFCC-700 specifies ("between the category component and the footer"). **SFCC-700 duplicates SFCC-90's final module.** SFCC-90 *is* a Level-2 page story by 04.71's definition — it is just monolithic rather than one-per-module.

So: adopting 04.71 requires deciding whether SFCC-90 is decomposed into per-module page stories (in which case SFCC-700 is one of its children) or stays whole (in which case SFCC-700 must not exist). **This is the most consequential open question for tomorrow** and 04.71 doesn't address what happens to existing page stories.

Related: **SFCC-94 "Homepage Content Row — Flexible Grid & Image Carousel"** (Squad-B) is a single story covering both the Contentful configuration *and* the PWA render — under 04.71 it should be two. It also makes column count (2/3/4) configurable, overlapping Editorial Cards' 1/2-column configuration. Two components solving column-count configurability in different ways is exactly the component-reuse gap flagged in the Exec Readout; worth checking whether Editorial Cards is a *variant of* SFCC-94's content row rather than a new module.

### 7.3 Misfiled and missing epics
- **SFCC-99 and SFCC-100 (Footer stories) sit in the Homepage epic.** The Footer is global chrome — 04.7's own Templates table puts it under **Shell**, and `protectedFiles.md` classes it as Tier 2 *Global Shell*. Footer content appears on every page.
- **There is no Shell epic in Jira**, though 04.7 defines a Shell template (Navigation, Logo Masthead, Disclaimer, Footer). Recommend creating one, or agreeing that Navigation (SFCC-3) absorbs it.
- **SFCC-111 "Promotional Announcement Banner — Contentful"** is a Contentful *component* story sitting in the Homepage page epic rather than SFCC-304 — the same misfile as SFCC-698, in a real story. Its content is good; only the parent is wrong.

---

## 8. Recommendations

### 8.1 Amend 04.71
1. Add the **Contentful pattern column** (Entry-driven vs Studio Experiences) and the story-order table from §4. This is the direct answer to the meeting's question.
2. Add the **field-ID contract table** (§5.2) as a required section in both stories of every Contentful pair.
3. Add the **sub-component rule** (§5.3): no separate story unless independently reusable.
4. State that 04.71 governs **decomposition only**; format stays 274137093 + Guide 1 (§6).
5. State that the Contentful story delivers **schema + Studio registration, not authored content** (§6).
6. Add a line on **what happens to existing monolithic page stories** (§7.2).

### 8.2 Fix the exemplars (or replace them)
Given SFCC-698's content model can't express its own variants, the fastest path is to **re-cut the example on a component that is design-confirmed**, and promote **SFCC-648** to the reference example for Level 1 / PWA Kit and **SFCC-51 → SFCC-111** for a Contentful pair. If Editorial Cards is kept:
- Reparent SFCC-698 → SFCC-304; SFCC-700 → SFCC-706.
- Strip render AC from SFCC-698, leaving content model / field IDs / validation / localisation.
- Resolve the card-collection question (container + `children`, vs repeating fields, vs entry references) and the missing column-count field.
- Split SFCC-699 AC1; add degradation, empty-state and image-performance AC.
- Fix SFCC-700's PLP/Homepage contradiction, the "footer above" error, and replace px with spacing tokens.
- Populate labels, Functional Area, Squad, Rollout Scope, Dependencies on all three — copy SFCC-648's pattern.
- Repoint SFCC-698's Title-and-Link references from SFCC-691 to SFCC-692.

### 8.3 A bonus the split gives you free — test-layer alignment
The two levels map cleanly onto this repo's three test layers (`.claude/rules/testing.md`), which makes the split pay for itself in QA:

| Story level | Test layer | Artefact |
|---|---|---|
| Level 1 — component (PWA Kit) | Vitest + Storybook `play` | `index.test.ts`, `index.stories.tsx` (title `Contentful/…` for CMS-driven, with mock Contentful data) |
| Level 1 — component (Contentful) | Schema drift check | `npm run generate:contentful:check` / content-type sync in CI (SFCC-322) |
| Level 2 — page | Playwright E2E | `.feature` + spec tagged `@homepage` / `@pdp` / `@plp` |

Note the E2E `@area` tags are `homepage, checkout, search, account, pdp, plp, integrations` — **page-shaped, with no component-level area.** That is further evidence the E2E gate belongs on Level-2 stories only, and that Level-1 stories should carry Storybook/Vitest AC instead. Only `e2e_homepage` is currently mapped in `qa.yml`; adding a new area's first spec requires its own allow-list group there.

Practical note: `qa-generate` needs a Jira key tag (`@SFCC-NNN`) per spec for Zephyr/BrowserStack scoping — so **Level-2 page stories are the ones that should carry E2E coverage**, and a Level-1 component story should not expect a BrowserStack run.

---

## 9. Questions to settle in the meeting

1. **Editorial Cards: entry-driven or Studio Experiences?** Determines story order and whether the current SFCC-698 model is viable at all. *(§4)*
2. **How is a multi-card module modelled** — container with child slots, repeating fields, or entry references? Blocks development regardless of answer. *(§3 #4)*
3. **Does SFCC-90 get decomposed** into per-module page stories, or does SFCC-700-style story not exist? *(§7.2)*
4. **Which story format wins** — 274137093 or Guide 1? Two incompatible templates are in circulation. *(§6)*
5. **Do sub-components get their own stories?** Four Footer sub-components hang on this. *(§5.3)*
6. **Who owns the field-ID contract** and where does it live — both stories, or a Confluence child page referenced by both? *(§5.2)*
7. **What Functional Area value does a Level-1 component story take?** The picklist is page-shaped (PDP / Home Page / PLP / Search / Integration). SFCC-648 pragmatically uses `PDP` for a component story — is "primary consuming page" the rule, or is a new value needed?

---

- **Confluence:** 400195600 (04.71) · 400195591 (04.7 Component Inventory, v13) · 274137093 (Creating User Stories with Claude, v11) · 277577757 (Guide 1, v2) · 313884676 (Definition of Done, v4) · 303071234 (04.1.1 Homepage & Content, HPC) · 303333385 (04.1.18 Storefront Page Templates)

# Review — Component User Stories & the Contentful ⇄ PWA Kit Dependency

**Prepared for:** "Contentful v PWA Kit Components and User Story Alignment" (Isabel Chaloner, Tim Lavelle)
**Date:** 2026-08-12 · **Reviewer:** Marcel Navarro (FE lead)
**Scope reviewed:** Confluence 04.71 (the assumed standard) · Confluence 04.7 Component Inventory · the six sample stories (SFCC-698/699/700, SFCC-92/648/650) · the earlier example set (SFCC-691/692/694) · Jira epic structure · the two pre-existing story standards · `.docs/integration/02-contentful.md` · the actual Contentful integration code in this repo.

---

## 1. Verdict

**The taxonomy in 04.71 is sound and worth adopting. The worked example chosen to demonstrate it (Editorial Cards) does not follow it, and — more importantly — the dependency direction 04.71 assumes is backwards for roughly half the Contentful components in this codebase.**

Three things need deciding before this pattern is rolled out across Sprint 3's story-writing effort:

1. **Which Contentful integration pattern a component uses** determines whether the Contentful story comes before or after the PWA Kit story. 04.71 assumes one order; the code supports two. (§4 — this is the substantive finding.)
2. **The Contentful story and the PWA Kit story need a shared, explicit field contract** or they cannot be worked independently. None of the six samples has one. (§5.2)
3. **Existing monolithic page stories (SFCC-90, SFCC-94) already cover the same ground** as the new Level-2 example. Adopting 04.71 without deciding what happens to them creates duplicate scope. (§7.2)

The best story in the sample set is **SFCC-648** — it is the only one with complete metadata and a named, owned dependency. It should be the template, not Editorial Cards.

---

## 2. What 04.71 gets right

Worth stating plainly, because most of this review is corrections:

- The two-level split (component epic / page epic) is the correct decomposition and matches where this codebase's test layers naturally sit (§8.3).
- "A Contentful component always needs a PWA Kit story too, because PWA Kit has to render it" is exactly right and is the single most useful sentence on the page.
- Writing Level-2 from the shopper's perspective, and explicitly *not* repeating build detail, is the right instinct.
- The classification is already pre-populated in 04.7 Component Inventory's "PWA Kit / Contentful" column, so the standard has a data source to drive it. That's more than most story conventions start with.

---

## 3. The sample stories — defect table

Verified against the two pre-existing standards (Confluence 274137093 *Creating User Stories with Claude* v11, and 277577757 *Guide 1: Writing Stories & AC*).

| # | Story | Finding | Severity |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | SFCC-698/699/700 | **All three sit in epic SFCC-2 "PWA Kit Components"** (verified `parent` field, not just the description text). Per 04.71, SFCC-698 belongs in **SFCC-304 Contentful Components** and SFCC-700 in a page epic (**SFCC-706 Homepage**, created 2026-08-12). Both target epics already exist. | High |
| 2 | SFCC-698 | **8 of 10 AC are render assertions, not content-model assertions.** AC2–AC8 are all phrased "*When the component renders on the storefront → Then …*". 04.71 assigns rendering to the PWA Kit story and the content model / authoring fields / validation rules to the Contentful story. The example inverts its own rule, and duplicates SFCC-699. | **High** |
| 3 | SFCC-698 | **The content model cannot express the four variants the Inventory lists.** 04.7 records Editorial Cards variants as *Editorial Cards / 2 Columns / Centered Text / 2 Columns Centered Text* — a 2×2 matrix of column-count × text-alignment. AC1 defines a single `Layout: Standard \| Centred text` enum and **no column-count field**. As specified, 2-column is unbuildable. | **High** |
| 4 | SFCC-698 | **No field defines the card collection.** AC1 lists one card's fields (single Image, single Body copy); AC3 requires "two cards side by side, each with their own independently configured content". Nothing in the model says whether Editorial Cards is a container holding 1–2 card entries, or one entry with duplicated field sets. This is the decision that blocks development. | **High** |
| 5 | SFCC-698 | **AC1 and AC9 both cite SFCC-691 for the Title and Link dependency.** SFCC-691 is the *PWA Kit render* story; **SFCC-692** is the Contentful content-model story. A content-model dependency must point at SFCC-692. | Medium |
| 6 | SFCC-698 | **An open question is embedded inside AC1**: "Image (required) — *from Contentful for editorial?*". Per 274137093 open items belong in Dependencies (`customfield_10232`) with a named owner, never inline in AC. Same defect in SFCC-692's description ("TBC: are these responsive designs, or different configurations?"). | Medium |
| 7 | SFCC-699 | **AC1 is a compound assertion covering ~16 combinations** — 4 fields × 2 layouts × 2 alignments in one criterion. Guide 1 lists "Compound Then" as a named common mistake: *"One failure masks the others in test results."* Needs splitting. | Medium |

AGENTS.md sets LCP ≤ 2s p75 mobile. A full-width editorial image module is squarely on that budget. | **High** |
| 10 | SFCC-700 | **Page contradiction.** Summary says "Homepage Template"; the story sentence says "*As a shopper browsing the product listing page*"; all four AC say homepage. SFCC-698 meanwhile scopes the component to "the Home page and PLP" — which under 04.71 requires **two** Level-2 stories, one per page. Only one exists, and it names the wrong page. | High |
| 11 | SFCC-700 | **AC3 is internally contradictory**: "*16px spacing between the Editorial Card and the footer **above***". AC2 already places the category component above. The footer is below. | Low |

Every real story carries these; SFCC-111 uses exactly `Contentful;Custom;HPC-017;Squad-A`. Without Req IDs these stories are invisible to the 04.1.x requirements-coverage trace. | High |
| 15 | SFCC-698/699/700 | **`**Epic:** PWA Kit Components` is written into the Description.** 274137093: the description must contain *only* the user story and context; epic is a field. SFCC-700 additionally has broken escaping (`\*\*Epic:\*\*`) so it renders as literal asterisks. | Low |
| 16 | SFCC-698 | Persona is "*merchandiser*"; the canonical persona in 04.3 / 274137093 is **Site Merchandiser** (as used correctly in SFCC-111 and SFCC-94). | Low |
| 17 | SFCC-699/700 | **No region tagging.** Guide 1: *"Always tag, even if the answer is [ALL]."* With one Contentful Space serving 8 storefronts across 11 locales (`02-contentful.md` §7) and the `regions` filtering field still an **open item** (§10.1), an untagged editorial component is a real ambiguity, not a formality. | Medium |
| 18 | SFCC-92/648/650 | **This set is materially better** and largely already complies. SFCC-92 was correctly thinned to page-level assembly and left in SFCC-5; 648/650 were split into SFCC-2 as component stories — exactly 04.71's model, arrived at independently in the SFCC-92 thread (Tim Lavelle 2026-07-26 → Jasmijn Tsang 2026-08-07). One correction: SFCC-648's description commits to **WCAG 2.1 AA**, but AGENTS.md targets **2.2 AA**, falling back to 2.1 only where 2.2 is infeasible *and documented*. | Medium |

---

## 4. The substantive finding — dependency direction is not uniform

04.71 states the Contentful story covers "the content model, authoring fields, configuration options and validation rules" and the PWA Kit story covers "how the component renders and responds to what Contentful delivers". That implies: **Contentful model first → PWA Kit renders it.**

That is correct for one of the two Contentful patterns in this repo, and backwards for the other.

### Pattern A — entry-driven components
`overrides/app/components/contentful/` — `heroBanner.tsx`, `duplexSection.tsx`, `videoEmbed.tsx`, `productHero.tsx`

- Receive a **typed Contentful entry/asset** as a prop (`ContentfulAsset` from `overrides/app/types/contentful`).
- Content types are defined in code and synced via `npm run sync:contentful` (`scripts/contentful/content-types/`, `scripts/contentful/migrations/`).
- Live Preview wiring is per-field: `ContentfulLivePreview.getProps({entryId, fieldId, locale})`.
- **The Contentful content model is genuinely upstream. 04.71's ordering is correct.**
- Critical constraint: `02-contentful.md` §2 — the sync script is **additive only, it never deletes a field from a live content type**. Getting the model wrong is expensive and semi-permanent. This is the strongest possible argument for reviewing the Contentful story *against real component prop needs* before it is built.

### Pattern B — Studio Experiences components
`overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/` — `collectionHero.tsx`, `imageText.tsx`, `shoppableImage.tsx`

- The authoring model is **generated from the React component's props**. You annotate the `Props` type with `@cf` JSDoc tags and run `npm run generate:contentful`, which rewrites `definitions.ts` (autogenerated; a pre-commit hook keeps it in sync).
- So the "content model / authoring fields" **are an output of writing the React component**, not an input to it. For these components 04.71's ordering is inverted.
- **And the available controls are severely limited.** `scripts/contentful/generateDefinitions.mjs` `CONTROL_MAP` supports exactly six: `shortText`, `longText`, `select`, `toggle`, `number`, `media` → mapping only to Contentful `Text`, `Boolean`, `Number`, `Media`.
  - **No reference/link control** → the "Title and Link sub-component (optional)" in SFCC-698 AC1 is not expressible.
  - **No array/repeater control** → "two cards, each independently configured" is not expressible.
  - **No rich text control.**
  - The existing workaround is visible and unattractive: `shoppableImage` degrades structured hotspot data to a **`Hotspots (JSON)` Text field** in Studio (a merchandiser hand-typing JSON), while the *content-type* version of the same component models it properly as an `Object`.
  - The one supported composition primitive is `children` → `children: true` on the registration. A 2-column Editorial Cards is therefore most naturally **a container component with two child slots**, each holding a single Editorial Card — not one entry with a layout enum.

### Why this matters for the meeting

**Editorial Cards as specified in SFCC-698 cannot be built as a Studio Experiences component today.** It needs either the entry-driven path with proper entry references, or re-decomposition into `editorialCard` + a layout container. That is a story-shape decision, not an implementation detail, and it has to be made before the story is estimated.

**Recommendation:** add a third column to the 04.71 quick-reference and to 04.7 Component Inventory — not just *PWA Kit / Contentful*, but *which Contentful pattern*: `Entry-driven` or `Studio Experiences`. Then:

| Pattern | Story order | Contentful story delivers | PWA Kit story delivers |
|---|---|---|---|
| Entry-driven | **Contentful first**, PWA Kit second | Content type in `content-types/` + migration, field IDs, validation, locale/region behaviour | Typed component consuming the entry, all render states |
| Studio Experiences | **PWA Kit first** (build against mock content in Storybook), Contentful second | `@cf` annotations reviewed, `definitions.ts` regenerated, Studio registration verified | Component + props, which *are* the authoring surface |

The project has already been doing the second one informally and correctly: **SFCC-51** built the Promotional Announcement Banner UI with mock content, and **SFCC-111** followed up with "the Contentful content model and the integration between Contentful and the PWA Kit component". SFCC-90 and SFCC-94 both say the component "can be built with mock content prior to Contentful content model being finalised." 04.71 should **codify that existing practice**, not contradict it.

> One guardrail worth writing into the DoD: mock Contentful content belongs in the `.stories.tsx` file only (`.claude/rules/components.md` explicitly endorses this for the `Contentful/` story category). AGENTS.md's "No mocking" rule still bars fixtures from production paths.

---

## 5. What's missing from 04.71

### 5.1 No AC format, no field guidance, no template
04.71 defines *how many* stories and *whose perspective*, but not what a story must contain. The result is visible in the samples: six exemplars with no labels, no Functional Area, no Squad, no Rollout Scope, no Dependencies, and an AC format (`**AC1 — title**` + Given/When/Then bullets) that matches neither existing standard. 04.71 should either adopt one of the two existing formats by reference or explicitly supersede them (§6).

### 5.2 The missing artefact — the field-ID contract
This is the highest-value addition and it directly answers "we are not 100% clear on how to structure these."

`02-contentful.md` §2: *"Each content type pairs with a typed React component. TypeScript types match the Contentful field IDs exactly, so schema drift is caught at compile time."*

That exact-match requirement is a **hard interface between the two stories** and neither SFCC-698 nor SFCC-699 records it — they use prose display names ("Body copy") with no field IDs. Every Contentful component pair should carry an identical table in both stories:

| Field ID | Display name | Type / control | Required | Localised | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `image` | Image | Media | Yes | No | |
| `imageAlt` | Image Alt Text | shortText | No | Yes | empty → `alt=""` |
| `bodyCopy` | Body Copy | longText | No | Yes | |
| `ctaLabel` | CTA Label | shortText | No | Yes | CTA renders only if label **and** URL set |
| `ctaUrl` | CTA URL | shortText | No | No | internal → same tab; external → `_blank` + `rel="noopener noreferrer"` |
| `textAlignment` | Text Alignment | select (`standard` \| `centred`) | Yes (default `standard`) | No | |

Once this table exists and is agreed, the Contentful story and the PWA Kit story are genuinely independently workable — which is the whole point of splitting them. Without it they will drift, and with an additive-only sync script the drift is expensive.

### 5.3 Sub-components are unaddressed
04.7 Inventory uses a `↳ Sub-component` type (Pause/Play, Footer Item, Image Gallery, Wishlist Icon…). 04.71 is silent on them. This repo's own convention already answers it — `.claude/rules/components.md`: *"Not required for purely internal sub-components that only render inside one parent… Cover their variants via the parent's stories."* Recommend: **sub-components do not get their own story unless they are independently reusable**; otherwise they are AC on the parent. Without this rule the Footer alone generates four stories (Footer, Footer Item, Footer Textfield, Icons).

### 5.4 The Inventory's vocabulary doesn't match the taxonomy
04.71 defines two component types. 04.7's column uses three values inconsistently: `PWA Kit`, `Contentful`, and — for Link only — `PWA Kit & Contentful`. But per 04.71 *every* Contentful component also needs a PWA Kit story, so Banner, Footer, Navigation, Editorial Cards, Title and Link, Logo Masthead and Disclaimer (all marked plain `Contentful`) each need two stories. The column that should mechanically tell a BA how many stories to write currently doesn't. Recommend aligning the Inventory to 04.71's exact labels: `PWA Kit only` / `Contentful + PWA Kit`.

### 5.5 Inventory data gaps that block story writing
- **Editorial Cards has `Pages: —`** — the component being used as the worked example has no page mapping, so you cannot derive which Level-2 stories are needed. (SFCC-698 says Home + PLP; SFCC-700 says Homepage; neither is in the Inventory.)
- **Editorial Cards and Title and Link are both 🟠 Not Confirmed** in design status — a component with unconfirmed designs was chosen as the pattern exemplar.
- **Templates table covers only Shell and PDP.** Homepage and PLP templates are absent, yet Level-2 stories are being written against both.

---

## 6. Governance collision — four overlapping standards

04.71 does not reference, and partially conflicts with, three existing pages:

| Page | Status | Conflict with 04.71 / the samples |
|---|---|---|
| **274137093 Creating User Stories with Claude** (v11, Jul 2026) | Detailed, field-level, actively used | Mandates Description = story + context only (samples put Epic in the description); AC as numbered `1. Given/When/Then` in `customfield_10231`; labels `Req-ID;Custom;Squad-X`; Functional Area / Squad / Rollout Scope / Dependencies all required. Samples satisfy none of these. |
| **277577757 Guide 1: Writing Stories & AC** (v2) | Zephyr-facing, defines the `AC Approved` gate | Prescribes a **different Description template entirely** (User Role / Goal / Context / In Scope / Out of Scope / Regions / Edge Cases / Story Key) and a different AC format (`AC-01: title [REGION]`). Samples match neither this nor 274137093. |
| **313884676 Definition of Done** | Applies to both squads | Requires "API Contracts Tested" and "Documentation updated". For a Contentful pair, "API contract" = the field-ID table in §5.2. Worth naming explicitly. |
| **400195600 04.71** | New | Adds a taxonomy but no format; silent on the above. |

**Recommendation:** 04.71 should state in one line that it governs *decomposition only* (how many stories, which epic, whose perspective) and that story *format* remains 274137093 + Guide 1. Then reconcile those two with each other separately — that conflict predates this meeting and is worth its own decision.

### One scope boundary to handle carefully
274137093 lists **"Content authoring in Contentful"** under *"Flag the following in open items but do not build"* (Accenture scope ends at SFCC + PWA Kit + SFCC-side integrations).

This does **not** invalidate 04.71's Contentful story — building the content *model* is in scope (`02-contentful.md` §2 puts schema in this repo, PR-reviewed). But SFCC-698 is phrased as an authoring activity by a Zimmermann persona ("*As a merchandiser, I want to configure Editorial Card modules in Contentful*"), which straddles the line. Recommend 04.71 add: **the Contentful story's deliverable is the content type + Studio registration, not authored entries.** The Site Merchandiser persona describes the capability being enabled; DoD is "content type deployed, component registered and configurable in Studio", never "content authored".

---

## 7. Backlog structure

### 7.1 Epic distribution is inverted
| Epic | Children | Note |
|---|---|---|
| **SFCC-2 PWA Kit Components** | 10 | **6 are EXAMPLE stories.** Only 4 real: SFCC-116, SFCC-236, SFCC-648, SFCC-650 |
| **SFCC-304 Contentful Components** | 4 | SFCC-306, 316, 326, 674 — and *none* of the Contentful exemplars |
| **SFCC-706 Homepage** | 7 | Created 2026-08-12 |

The component epics are nearly empty while page epics hold the real work — i.e. the codebase is currently organised the *old* way, and 04.71 describes a target state that hasn't been migrated to. That migration is the actual Sprint 3 task, and it is much larger than writing three example stories.

Housekeeping: the six `EXAMPLE:` stories are documentation living in a delivery epic. They will be picked up by sprint reports and epic burn-up. Move them to a dedicated epic, label them `example`, or convert them to a Confluence child page of 04.71.

### 7.2 Duplication with existing stories — needs a decision
**SFCC-90 "Homepage Layout & Content Modules UI"** (In Refinement, HPC-008/009, Shopper persona) already enumerates every homepage module top-to-bottom, ending with:

> *"Editorial and/or boutique duo — a final row containing two equal-width (for desktop) hero images side by side: one linking to an editorial destination and one linking to the boutiques page or store locator."*

That is the 2-Column Editorial Card, in the same page position SFCC-700 specifies ("between the category component and the footer"). **SFCC-700 duplicates SFCC-90's final module.** SFCC-90 *is* a Level-2 page story by 04.71's definition — it is just monolithic rather than one-per-module.

So: adopting 04.71 requires deciding whether SFCC-90 is decomposed into per-module page stories (in which case SFCC-700 is one of its children) or stays whole (in which case SFCC-700 must not exist). **This is the most consequential open question for tomorrow** and 04.71 doesn't address what happens to existing page stories.

Related: **SFCC-94 "Homepage Content Row — Flexible Grid & Image Carousel"** (Squad-B) is a single story covering both the Contentful configuration *and* the PWA render — under 04.71 it should be two. It also makes column count (2/3/4) configurable, overlapping Editorial Cards' 1/2-column configuration. Two components solving column-count configurability in different ways is exactly the component-reuse gap flagged in the Exec Readout; worth checking whether Editorial Cards is a *variant of* SFCC-94's content row rather than a new module.

### 7.3 Misfiled and missing epics
- **SFCC-99 and SFCC-100 (Footer stories) sit in the Homepage epic.** The Footer is global chrome — 04.7's own Templates table puts it under **Shell**, and `protectedFiles.md` classes it as Tier 2 *Global Shell*. Footer content appears on every page.
- **There is no Shell epic in Jira**, though 04.7 defines a Shell template (Navigation, Logo Masthead, Disclaimer, Footer). Recommend creating one, or agreeing that Navigation (SFCC-3) absorbs it.
- **SFCC-111 "Promotional Announcement Banner — Contentful"** is a Contentful *component* story sitting in the Homepage page epic rather than SFCC-304 — the same misfile as SFCC-698, in a real story. Its content is good; only the parent is wrong.

---

## 8. Recommendations

### 8.1 Amend 04.71
1. Add the **Contentful pattern column** (Entry-driven vs Studio Experiences) and the story-order table from §4. This is the direct answer to the meeting's question.
2. Add the **field-ID contract table** (§5.2) as a required section in both stories of every Contentful pair.
3. Add the **sub-component rule** (§5.3): no separate story unless independently reusable.
4. State that 04.71 governs **decomposition only**; format stays 274137093 + Guide 1 (§6).
5. State that the Contentful story delivers **schema + Studio registration, not authored content** (§6).
6. Add a line on **what happens to existing monolithic page stories** (§7.2).

### 8.2 Fix the exemplars (or replace them)
Given SFCC-698's content model can't express its own variants, the fastest path is to **re-cut the example on a component that is design-confirmed**, and promote **SFCC-648** to the reference example for Level 1 / PWA Kit and **SFCC-51 → SFCC-111** for a Contentful pair. If Editorial Cards is kept:
- Reparent SFCC-698 → SFCC-304; SFCC-700 → SFCC-706.
- Strip render AC from SFCC-698, leaving content model / field IDs / validation / localisation.
- Resolve the card-collection question (container + `children`, vs repeating fields, vs entry references) and the missing column-count field.
- Split SFCC-699 AC1; add degradation, empty-state and image-performance AC.
- Fix SFCC-700's PLP/Homepage contradiction, the "footer above" error, and replace px with spacing tokens.
- Populate labels, Functional Area, Squad, Rollout Scope, Dependencies on all three — copy SFCC-648's pattern.
- Repoint SFCC-698's Title-and-Link references from SFCC-691 to SFCC-692.

### 8.3 A bonus the split gives you free — test-layer alignment
The two levels map cleanly onto this repo's three test layers (`.claude/rules/testing.md`), which makes the split pay for itself in QA:

| Story level | Test layer | Artefact |
|---|---|---|
| Level 1 — component (PWA Kit) | Vitest + Storybook `play` | `index.test.ts`, `index.stories.tsx` (title `Contentful/…` for CMS-driven, with mock Contentful data) |
| Level 1 — component (Contentful) | Schema drift check | `npm run generate:contentful:check` / content-type sync in CI (SFCC-322) |
| Level 2 — page | Playwright E2E | `.feature` + spec tagged `@homepage` / `@pdp` / `@plp` |

Note the E2E `@area` tags are `homepage, checkout, search, account, pdp, plp, integrations` — **page-shaped, with no component-level area.** That is further evidence the E2E gate belongs on Level-2 stories only, and that Level-1 stories should carry Storybook/Vitest AC instead. Only `e2e_homepage` is currently mapped in `qa.yml`; adding a new area's first spec requires its own allow-list group there.

Practical note: `qa-generate` needs a Jira key tag (`@SFCC-NNN`) per spec for Zephyr/BrowserStack scoping — so **Level-2 page stories are the ones that should carry E2E coverage**, and a Level-1 component story should not expect a BrowserStack run.

---

## 9. Questions to settle in the meeting

1. **Editorial Cards: entry-driven or Studio Experiences?** Determines story order and whether the current SFCC-698 model is viable at all. *(§4)*
2. **How is a multi-card module modelled** — container with child slots, repeating fields, or entry references? Blocks development regardless of answer. *(§3 #4)*
3. **Does SFCC-90 get decomposed** into per-module page stories, or does SFCC-700-style story not exist? *(§7.2)*
4. **Which story format wins** — 274137093 or Guide 1? Two incompatible templates are in circulation. *(§6)*
5. **Do sub-components get their own stories?** Four Footer sub-components hang on this. *(§5.3)*
6. **Who owns the field-ID contract** and where does it live — both stories, or a Confluence child page referenced by both? *(§5.2)*
7. **What Functional Area value does a Level-1 component story take?** The picklist is page-shaped (PDP / Home Page / PLP / Search / Integration). SFCC-648 pragmatically uses `PDP` for a component story — is "primary consuming page" the rule, or is a new value needed?

Full review written to [componentStoryReview.md](.docs/temp/componentStoryReview.md). Here's what matters.

## The headline

**04.71's taxonomy is sound. The example chosen to demonstrate it is the wrong example, and the dependency direction it assumes is backwards for half the Contentful components in this repo.**

## The substantive finding

There are **two** Contentful patterns in the codebase with **opposite** dependency directions:

- **Entry-driven** ([heroBanner.tsx](overrides/app/components/contentful/heroBanner.tsx) etc.) — content type synced from `content-types/`, component consumes a typed entry. **04.71's order is correct: Contentful first.** And the sync is *additive-only* — a wrong field can't be deleted later, so the model genuinely must be agreed up front.
- **Studio Experiences** ([experiences/](overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/)) — the authoring model is **generated from the React props** via `@cf` JSDoc → `definitions.ts`. The "content model / authoring fields" are an *output* of building the component. **04.71's order is inverted here.**

And the codegen's `CONTROL_MAP` supports only six controls (Text/Boolean/Number/Media). No reference, no array, no rich text. So:

> **Editorial Cards as written in SFCC-698 cannot be built as a Studio Experiences component.** Its "Title and Link sub-component" needs an entry reference; "two cards, each independently configured" needs a repeater. Neither exists. The precedent workaround is `shoppableImage`, which degrades structured data to a `Hotspots (JSON)` text box a merchandiser hand-types.

The project is already doing the PWA-first order correctly and informally — SFCC-51 built the banner UI with mock content, SFCC-111 followed with the content model. SFCC-90 and SFCC-94 both say the same. **04.71 should codify that, not contradict it.**

## Highest-value gaps in the sample stories

1. **8 of SFCC-698's 10 AC are render assertions** ("*When the component renders on the storefront…*") — the Contentful story duplicates the PWA Kit story, inverting 04.71's own rule.
2. **The content model can't express its own variants.** 04.7 lists 4 variants (columns × alignment); AC1 defines one 2-value `Layout` enum and **no column-count field**.
3. **All three sit in `SFCC-2 PWA Kit Components`** — verified `parent` field. `SFCC-304` and `SFCC-706` both already exist.
4. **`Functional Area`, `Squad`, `Rollout Scope`, `Dependencies` are empty on all three**, and none have labels — so no Req ID traceability. Compare **SFCC-648**, which has all of it plus a named @Kiera dependency. That's your template, not Editorial Cards.
5. **The missing artefact:** a shared **field-ID contract table**. `02-contentful.md` §2 requires TS types to match Contentful field IDs *exactly*; neither story records a single field ID. Without it the two stories can't be worked independently — which is the entire point of splitting them.

## Two things you'll want to raise that aren't on the agenda

- **SFCC-700 duplicates SFCC-90.** SFCC-90 already specifies *"Editorial and/or boutique duo — a final row containing two equal-width hero images side by side"* in the same page position. SFCC-90 **is** a Level-2 story, just monolithic. Adopting 04.71 means deciding whether SFCC-90 gets decomposed — it's the most consequential open question and 04.71 is silent on it.
- **04.71 is the fourth overlapping story standard.** [274137093](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/274137093) (v11) and [Guide 1](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/277577757) prescribe **two incompatible Description templates and two AC formats**; the samples match neither. Suggest 04.71 declare itself decomposition-only and leave format to those.

One scope nuance worth handling gently: 274137093 lists *"Content authoring in Contentful"* as out of Accenture scope. That doesn't invalidate the Contentful story — building the *schema* is in scope — but SFCC-698 is phrased as merchandiser authoring. Worth one clarifying line: the deliverable is the content type + Studio registration, not authored entries.

Smaller confirmed defects: SFCC-700 says "*shopper browsing the product listing page*" under a Homepage summary; its AC3 places the footer "above"; its 40px/16px values violate the Chakra-token rule; SFCC-698 cites SFCC-691 (render story) for a content-model dependency when it means SFCC-692; SFCC-699 AC1 compounds ~16 combinations into one criterion and has no AC for Contentful-unavailable or image performance despite both being mandated in `02-contentful.md`.

I've also flagged a side issue as a task chip — `heroBanner.tsx` has a `console.error` and an external `via.placeholder.com` fallback, both against project rules. Unrelated to the stories, but it's on a hero image and therefore on the LCP budget.

meeting 1 notes:

This recap focuses on what was actually discussed, what decisions are emerging, and most importantly, what responsibilities appear to be landing with you as Frontend Development (FED) Lead.
Executive Summary
The meeting was intended to align the team on how to write stories for Contentful and PWA Kit work, but the discussion quickly expanded into:

* Component ownership
* Story decomposition
* Dependency management
* Estimation accuracy
* Design system governance
* Salesforce/PWA Kit reuse

The emerging model is:

* Page stories describe the user journey and business outcome.
* Component stories describe implementation details, behavior, and accessibility.
* Contentful stories describe content configuration and authoring concerns.
* Feature stories depend on component stories, rather than containing all technical details themselves.

For you as FED Lead, the biggest takeaway is:
You are expected to be the technical validation layer between Figma → Jira Story → Engineering Implementation.
Key Discussion Areas
1. Establishing a Component-First Story Model
The meeting reviewed two example approaches:
Contentful Example

* Editorial Cards

PWA Example

* PDP Hero functionality
   * Size Selector
   * Add To Bag

The intent was to determine what belongs in:

* Contentful stories
* PWA Kit stories
* Page-level stories

The discussion consistently leaned toward creating dedicated component stories that can be reused, estimated, and tracked independently.
2. Separating Page Stories from Component Stories
The PDP example was used to demonstrate how a feature story should be broken apart.
Proposed Structure
Page Story
Contains:

* User journey
* Functional outcome
* Component interaction

Example:

* PDP purchasing experience

Component Stories
Contain:

* Component behavior
* Acceptance criteria
* Accessibility requirements

Examples:

* Size Selector
* Add To Bag

The page story would then reference those component stories as dependencies.
Why This Matters
This provides:

* Better estimation
* Better visibility of work
* Cleaner ownership boundaries
* Less duplication

3. Add To Bag Became a Key Architectural Discussion
A substantial portion of the meeting focused on whether Add To Bag is simply a button or its own component.
The discussion strongly favored:
✅ Treating Add To Bag as a component.
Reasoning included:

* Business rules
* Product state handling
* Inventory logic
* Cart interactions
* Size-selection dependencies

FED Implication
When decomposing work, don't classify commerce behaviors as basic UI elements simply because they visually resemble one.
A button may be visually simple while containing significant functional complexity underneath.
What Specifically Applies To You as FED Lead
1. Own Dependency Discovery During Refinement
This was probably the strongest expectation that emerged during the meeting.
The team repeatedly discussed how stories become underestimated when hidden dependencies are discovered too late.
Questions You Should Drive During Refinement
For every component story:

* Does a Salesforce component already exist?
* Does a PWA Kit equivalent already exist?
* Does an FE shared component already exist?
* Do the required atoms already exist?
* Do the required tokens already exist?

The emerging model is:

* Page stories describe the user journey and business outcome.
* Component stories describe implementation details, behavior, and accessibility.
* Contentful stories describe content configuration and authoring concerns.
* Feature stories depend on component stories, rather than containing all technical details themselves.

For you as FED Lead, the biggest takeaway is:
You are expected to be the technical validation layer between Figma → Jira Story → Engineering Implementation.

Contentful Example

PWA Example

* PDP Hero functionality

   * Add To Bag

The intent was to determine what belongs in:

* Contentful stories
* PWA Kit stories
* Page-level stories

The discussion consistently leaned toward creating dedicated component stories that can be reused, estimated, and tracked independently.
2. Separating Page Stories from Component Stories
The PDP example was used to demonstrate how a feature story should be broken apart.
Proposed Structure
Page Story
Contains:

* User journey
* Functional outcome
* Component interaction

Example:

* PDP purchasing experience

Component Stories
Contain:

* Component behavior
* Acceptance criteria
* Accessibility requirements

Examples:

* Size Selector
* Add To Bag

The page story would then reference those component stories as dependencies.

This provides:

* Better estimation
* Better visibility of work
* Cleaner ownership boundaries
* Less duplication

/**

 */

# Meeting 2 Prep — Component Stories, Reuse & FED Governance

**Context:** follow-up to "Contentful v PWA Kit Components and User Story Alignment" (meeting 1).
**Prepared:** 2026-08-12 · Marcel Navarro (FED Lead)
**Companion doc:** [componentStoryReview.md](./componentStoryReview.md) — the story-level review from before meeting 1.

---

## 1. The reframe to open with

Meeting 1 assigned FED Lead a list of things to *establish*: dependency validation, reuse discipline, component governance, PR review criteria, an atoms model, a refinement checklist.

**Most of it already exists in this repo and works. The gap is visibility, not capability.**

| Meeting 1 asked for | Status in repo | Real gap |
|---|---|---|
| "Does a Salesforce/PWA Kit/FE component already exist?" | ✅ `.claude/registry/components.md` — 82 rows, columns: **Component · Origin (Base/Override/Custom) · Path · Props · Tier · Squad · Consumers** | It lives in `.claude/` and is written for Claude. BAs refining stories never see it. |
| Registry accuracy | ✅ Auto-regenerated by `scripts/hooks/pre-commit` on any `overrides/app/{components,hooks,utils,pages,routes}` change, and staged automatically | Only triggers on *override* changes — a base-package version bump won't refresh it on its own |
| Reuse-first decision path | ✅ Encoded in AGENTS.md (**Copy-first rule**, **Minimal changes**, "Never refactor upward") | Not surfaced during refinement, only at implementation time |
| Accessibility enforced at review | ⚠️ Partial — 3 ast-grep rules only: `img-missing-alt`, `icon-button-missing-aria-label`, `clickable-non-interactive-element` | No enforcement of focus order, keyboard operability, or WCAG 2.2-specific criteria |
| "Tokens used? Hardcoded styling avoided?" | ❌ **Convention only.** `.claude/rules/css.md` states this outright: *"Not currently mechanically enforced"* — and names ast-grep as the fix | A real, cheap gap. See §6. |
| Complexity / duplication limits | ❌ Not enforced — confirmed no `complexity` / `max-lines-per-function` in `.eslintrc.js`; `components.md` already admits this | Same — cheap ESLint core addition, no new dependency |
| Atoms governance model | ✅ Largely exists — `components.md` story-required rule + the Storybook categorisation table (`Foundation/ Elements/ Layout/ Commerce/ Forms/ Pages/ Contentful`) | Needs restating in BA language, not invented from scratch |

**Position for meeting 2:** I'm not building a governance layer. I'm exposing the one that exists to the refinement conversation, and closing two named enforcement holes.

---

## 2. The reuse claim — verified, with paths

Meeting 1 asserted Size Selector and Add To Bag have existing Salesforce/PWA Kit equivalents. **Correct.** Specifics, so this stops being a process question and becomes a lookup:

| Story | Existing base implementation | What it already does |
|---|---|---|
| **SFCC-648** `pdp/size-selector` | `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/swatch-group/` (`index.jsx`, `swatch.jsx`, `index.test.js`) | Variant/attribute selection UI, per-swatch state, with an existing test |
| **SFCC-650** `pdp/add-to-bag` | `.../app/components/product-view/index.jsx` | **The full add-to-cart path already exists:** `addToCart([{product, variant, quantity}])` (L401), button render + label (L444), `useAddToCartModalContext` (L34), bundle handling via `isProductPartOfBundle` (L427), and an `updateCart` variant of the same button |
| **SFCC-196** max purchase quantity | `.../app/components/quantity-picker/` | Quantity control |
| Supporting hooks | `use-controlled-variations`, `use-derived-product`, `use-add-to-cart-modal` | Variant resolution and post-add modal |

**Consequence for SFCC-650 as currently written.** Its description says *"Cart API integration is in scope for this story"* — but `product-view` already performs the cart call. The story should say **extend/override `product-view`'s add-to-cart**, not build cart integration. As written it invites a parallel implementation of logic that ships in the base package.

---

## 3. The hidden dependency nobody has estimated

This is the concrete answer to Jasmijn's estimation concern, and it's the strongest thing to bring to meeting 2.

**Neither `swatch-group/` nor `product-view/` exists in `overrides/` yet.** Current contents of `overrides/app/components/`: `_app-config`, `button`, `contentful`, `header`, `icons`, `pageContainer`. That's it.

AGENTS.md's **Copy-first rule** therefore applies to both SFCC-648 and SFCC-650, and it is a serialised, human-gated step:

1. Copy each base file to the mirrored path in `overrides/`
2. Convert to TypeScript (`.ts`/`.tsx`) and fix imports — *strict rule: no `.js`/`.jsx` under `overrides/`*
3. `npx tsc --noEmit`
4. Add a temporary `console.log` marker to each copied file
5. **Stop. Wait for a human to confirm the override renders instead of the base component.**
6. Only then make functional changes; remove the markers

**Why it matters for estimation:** the first component story that touches a given base component carries a one-off override-scaffolding cost — including a hard pause for human verification — that subsequent stories against the same component do not. That cost is invisible in the Figma and invisible in the story. It is exactly the "story looked small until we found the prerequisite" pattern raised in meeting 1.

**Proposal:** make "override already scaffolded? (Y/N)" an explicit line in the refinement checklist. If N, either split the scaffolding into its own enabler story or size the first story accordingly. `.claude/registry/components.md`'s `Origin` column answers it in one glance — `Base` means not yet scaffolded.

> Related: `.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md` forward-declares Tier 2 paths that don't exist yet (`product-tile/`, `swatch-group/`, `order-summary/`, …). So a story's tier can't always be read off the filesystem — but the registry resolves a Tier for base components too (e.g. `DisplayPrice` → `2 — Protected`), so use the registry, not `ls`.

---

## 4. Add To Bag was already decided — two weeks ago

Meeting 1 spent "a substantial portion" concluding that Add To Bag is a component, not a button. That conclusion was reached and implemented before the meeting:

- **2026-07-26** — Tim Lavelle, on SFCC-92: *"My view is that the Size Selector and Add to Bag should be different components and user stories because some items won't have a size selector… The Add to Bag component will have some validation rules."*
- **2026-08-07** — Jasmijn Tsang, on SFCC-92: created **SFCC-648** and **SFCC-650** under SFCC-2, and thinned SFCC-92 to page-level assembly in SFCC-5. Verified: both stories exist, both parented to SFCC-2, both linked `blocks` → SFCC-92.

**This is a process finding, not a content one.** The decision was correct and is already built; it was re-derived because it lived in a Jira comment thread rather than anywhere refinement looks. Worth raising as the reason the registry/checklist needs to be *visible* — the same forces will re-litigate the next decision too.

* Homepage composition
* Cart/Cart Flyout experiences
* Recommendation modules
* Contentful preview workflows

Discussion Breakdown
1. Reviewing the Editorial Card User Story Approach
Isabel walked through how she has been writing Contentful stories.
Her approach was to:

* Identify all configurable content fields.
* Define content model acceptance criteria.
* Capture optional versus required fields.
* Define different configuration possibilities.

Examples discussed included:

* One-column/two-column layouts
* CTA enablement
* Body copy enablement
* Text alignment options

Tim reviewed the structure and indicated that the direction looked reasonable.
The conversation highlighted that some assumptions around optional vs required fields may still require design-team confirmation because certain components are not yet completely standardized.
2. Separating Contentful and PWA Responsibilities
A significant portion of the meeting focused on dividing ownership between Contentful stories and frontend rendering stories.
Contentful Stories
The group discussed Contentful stories as the place where teams should describe:

* content fields
* authoring requirements
* configurable properties
* supported component variations

PWA Kit Stories
The frontend stories should focus on:

* rendering behavior
* responsiveness
* accessibility
* CTA behavior
* navigation behavior
* user interaction expectations

The intent is to avoid duplicating the same requirements in both systems.
3. Accessibility and Rendering Guidance
While discussing editorial card rendering, accessibility considerations were raised.
The group talked through:

* image rendering
* accessibility handling
* alt text behavior

Tim specifically advised that when alt text is unavailable, the frontend should avoid rendering an unnecessary alt attribute rather than inserting placeholder values.
The team also discussed:

* responsive rendering
* CTA functionality
* accessibility expectations for component delivery

4. External Links Follow-Up
A small discussion occurred around link behavior.
Topics included:

* external links
* opening links in new tabs
* related link attributes

Tim mentioned uncertainty around one specific implementation detail and suggested a future follow-up rather than blocking current story creation.
No final decision was reached during this meeting.
5. Homepage Epic vs Component Stories
One of Isabel's main questions was how homepage work should be represented.
She described a concern that when all components are built independently, there may still need to be homepage-level stories to validate the final experience.
The discussion explored:

* homepage composition
* page assembly
* integration testing
* story organization

Tim's Guidance
Tim stated that developers should not generally need separate implementation stories for every homepage use case if:

* the reusable component already exists
* all supported variants have already been built

Using the editorial card example:

* Components should already support all required variations.
* When added to the homepage, authors should simply configure the component.
* Additional development should not be required each time a component is placed on a page.

The homepage therefore becomes more of a composition and validation exercise than a component-development effort.
6. Iterative Assembly and Validation Approach
The team discussed how pages should evolve during implementation.
Instead of waiting for all development to complete before validating pages, Tim suggested an incremental approach:

* Build components.
* Add completed components into real page compositions.
* Validate rendering as components become available.
* Continue building out pages progressively.

The goal is to discover issues earlier and continuously verify design alignment.
The discussion also covered eventual QA activities where testers validate:

* component settings
* rendering behavior
* spacing
* design fidelity

against the approved designs.
7. Cart / Cart Flyout Example
The discussion then shifted to a cart-related design.
The cart was examined as an example of a page that is actually made up of multiple reusable capabilities.
The group identified a number of different content types and modules within the cart experience, including:

* product-driven content
* pricing information
* payment-related experiences
* recommendation-style content
* marketing-focused content

The discussion reinforced that many of these elements could and should be represented as reusable components rather than bespoke cart-only functionality.
8. Recommendation and Merchandising Questions
The team then discussed recommendation-related content.
Examples mentioned included:

* Shop the Look
* Complete the Look
* Recommended for You style experiences

Questions were raised around:

* where recommendation data originates
* whether content is manually curated
* whether personalization mechanisms are involved

Bianca confirmed that certain recommendation experiences are manually curated.
The group also noted that some of the referenced screens were older designs and that newer designs will need to be reviewed before implementation decisions are finalized.
No final technical approach was agreed upon during the meeting.
Instead, additional clarification was identified as necessary.
9. Content Ownership Rule
Toward the end of the meeting, Tim provided what became the clearest architectural guideline of the session:
If content is not sourced from products or categories, it will generally live in Contentful.
This became the practical rule of thumb discussed by the group when deciding where content should be managed.
The statement was intended to help teams make content ownership decisions more consistently.
10. Preview and Publishing Workflow
The final discussion focused on how business users would validate content before publication.
The group discussed:

* Contentful preview capabilities
* Production preview experiences
* How content authors review changes before publishing

Tim explained that the intended workflow includes previewing content before publishing and using preview environments to validate changes before they become visible on the live website.
Questions were raised about whether staging environments are also used in the process, but no final workflow decision was captured in this section of the discussion.
Key Decisions
Agreed

* Component-first delivery model.
* Contentful stories describe content models and configuration.
* PWA stories describe rendering and behavior.
* Reusable components should support all documented variations.
* Homepage delivery should focus on composition and validation rather than duplicate development.
* Incremental page assembly and validation is preferred over waiting for complete delivery.
* Content not sourced from product/category data will generally be managed in Contentful.

Open Questions

* External-link implementation details.
* Recommendation module behavior.
* Personalization vs manual curation ownership.
* Final recommendation logic requirements.
* Certain merchandising-related flows.
* Some preview and publishing process details.

Overall Meeting Outcome"
